guitar.evidence: Trained knowledge: Gary Clark Jr. is well known for using semi-hollow guitars, notably an Epiphone Casino and later a signature Gibson/Epiphone ES-335-style model.
guitar.notes: Well-documented modern blues-rock guitarist gear — should not have been unknown.

tone.target: nasal wah-fuzz lead with gritty sustain
tone.profile: nasal wah-fuzz lead with gritty sustain
tone.summary: A gritty, fuzzy signal chain utilizing a pre-amp boost/OD, followed by a Wah filter, leading into the UK 45 amp model with a British cabinet, perfect for blues-rock leads.

rig.name: Gary Clark Jr. - When My Train Pulls In (Live) - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Slightly boost signal and emphasize mids for the 'mid-forward grind'.
blocks.gap: The Boost module is used to shape tone rather than provide primary gain, as requested by the fuzz/wah focus.

blocks.purpose: Provide the core 'fuzzy bite' and aggressive sustain.
Execute the required 'wah sweeps' and add vocal character.
Provide a classic British grit and mid-forward punch suitable for blues rock.
blocks.gap: The UK 45 is chosen over the UK 50 for its slightly more aggressive, focused tone that complements fuzz better.

blocks.purpose: Ground the sound with a classic British cabinet tone.
Added subtle movement for lead lines (optional). Kept inactive to avoid distracting from the core fuzz/wah sound.
blocks.gap: No specific modulation was requested, but Tremolo is a versatile addition that won't clash with the aggressive tone.

blocks.purpose: Provide a subtle sense of space and sustain without sounding overly processed.
blocks.gap: The 'drop delay' correction was implemented using the Digital Delay module for controlled, rhythmic repeats.

blocks.purpose: Add natural room ambience to the sustained leads.
blocks.gap: A subtle Room reverb is used to give depth without muddying the aggressive fuzz tone.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism to ground the aggressive fuzz/wah tone.

proposals.reason: The UK Vintage 4x12 is too British; a more American cab will better match the genre's grit and sustain.
